policy: Rules may group sources and describe optional local capture, conversion, or monitoring; every manifest entry does not need its own technical rule. For ordinary research, a human-reviewed official source link is sufficient after checking publisher, source identity, language, displayed date/version or cutoff, relevant passage, and visible caveats. Prefer a government-published consolidation; if none is usable, use the closest government-published text and state its cutoff and limits. Use Gazette fragments only for a specific material question; do not reconstruct a full amendment chain by default. Exact-byte storage, hashes, OCR, conversion, and replay checks apply only when retaining or reproducing a local copy, or when recurring monitoring genuinely needs them. External-reference use, local-copy acceptance, topic coverage, and country completion are separate. Do not bypass access controls or reuse terms.

rules.publisher_or_shape: Other authority pages, court indexes and official PDFs
rules.retrieval: For ordinary use, open the exact allowlisted official URL manually and record the review date, language, displayed version/date and the specific passage or page used. If storing a copy or monitoring it, use bounded TLS-validated retrieval and retain exact bytes/hash as appropriate; record access failures without bypass. A search page is not a case-law corpus.
rules.conversion: A source link needs no converter. If retaining text, use an observed source-specific HTML selector or review only the PDF pages used, including material attachments. Case-law indexes remain discovery surfaces; individual decisions and the covered court/date range must be identified before making a coverage claim.
rules.status: Some authority routes remain blocked or page shells. The rule 11/2025 index entry and appellate-decisions listing are directly reviewed as narrow official references; the individual rule text and judgment merits remain unverified. Local index copies are optional.

reference_use_policy: For every source type, prefer the responsible official publisher. Prefer a usable government-published consolidation for national legislation and the responsible EU publisher consolidation for EU legislation; if none is usable, use the closest government-published or official-service version and record its language, displayed date/cutoff, scope, and limits. A human-reviewed official link is enough for ordinary research; a custom capture/conversion rule, local copy, API, replay check, or updater is optional. Use Gazette fragments only to resolve a material question; do not reconstruct a full chain by default. Keep reference use, local-copy acceptance, topic coverage, and country completion separate.
